Hi Alex — thanks for sending this over and for the clear callouts. I pulled together initial answers and attached a short admin-controls summary and an example SCIM attribute mapping CSV to help your identity team review. High-level answers below; we can follow up with a technical deep-dive next week.

SCIM / provisioning
- Protocol: SCIM 2.0 (RFC7643/RFC7644) implementation.
- PATCH: supported (add/replace/remove semantics).
- Incremental sync: supported via changeTokens (we return startIndex & itemsPerPage for lists; changetoken for incremental updates).
- Groups: group push is supported; group-membership is represented as group resource with multi-valued members.
- Bulk: bulk endpoints are not enabled by default; we can enable for onboarding-sized jobs with staged throttles.
- Rate limits & recommendations: default tenant-level SCIM throughput is 600 requests/minute; for 18k users we typically recommend a staged import (bulk or parallel PUT/PATCH) followed by an hourly incremental sync. We can raise limits for Dedicated/Private deployments or during onboarding windows.

SAML / OIDC
- SSO: SAML 2.0 (IdP/SP) and OIDC (authorization code + PKCE) are both first-class.
- IdP-initiated vs SP-initiated: both supported; attribute mapping configurable per connection.
- NameID formats and attribute statements: support transient, persistent, and email-based identifiers.

RBAC & Admin delegation
- Roles: out-of-box roles include Org Admin, Identity Admin, Model Admin, Billing Admin, and Readonly Auditor.
- Custom roles: customers can create scoped custom roles limited to projects, models, or regions.
- Delegated admin: policy-based scoping allows granting subset privileges (e.g., user password reset, group management) without billing or model-level rights.

Audit & evidence
- Audit logs: user/admin action logs (login, token issuance, role changes, SCIM events) are captured in our audit stream. Default retention is 90 days; enterprise retention tiers (1 year, 7 years) are available through contract.
- Exports: CSV/JSON export and S3/Cloud Storage push available; we can also provide an on-prem archive for Private deployments.

Next steps: I’ll follow up with Ben on the SCIM sync sequencing notes and share a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) and sample evidence link. If you want a technical session, we have availability Tue/Wed next week.

Regards,

Alex — brief technical clarifications below (I pasted the SCIM sequence file as an attachment as well):

SCIM changetokens / determinism
- Sequence model: our SCIM service returns a changetoken (opaque string) with each list response and delta calls. The token increments monotonically per tenant and can be stored by clients as a checkpoint. We include an incremental index + time-based watermark so clients can assert ordering.
- Reconciliation: recommended pattern: checkpoint last changetoken after successful apply; if a resync is required, perform full list with startIndex=0 and then resume from subsequent change tokens.

Throttling / cadence
- Default 600 req/min tenant-level. For large org imports we offer an onboarding burst policy (up to 5k req/min for a 24–72 hour window) when coordinated. For Dedicated/Private we can set SLAs for sustained higher throughput.

PATCH / Bulk semantics
- PATCH semantics: add/replace/remove per RFC; we support single-resource PATCH and will support bulk PATCH in the onboarding toggle.
- Bulk: we support bulk PUT for initial imports; bulk PATCH for incremental group changes is in beta but can be enabled for POCs.

Role audit chain
- All role assignments include metadata: actor (user id + internal operator id if via API key), timestamp, and optional approvalId (if the change originates from an integrated approval tool). Audit entries are queryable via the audit API and included in export bundles.

Private deployments
- Private (VPC/on‑prem) feature parity: SCIM, SAML/OIDC, RBAC, and audit exports are functionally the same; retention/export options are more flexible (can push directly to your S3 or an on-prem archive). Installation options may change rate-limit defaults to match local infra.

I attached scim-sync-sequence.txt with a short example of delta flow and recommended checkpoint handling. Happy to run a short sync demo against a test tenant.

—Ben
Senior Product Manager, Identity — Redwood Inference
